compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

physical.finish: Black epoxy-polyester hybrid powder coat paint on steel parts; black plastic
physical.material: Steel mid panels and splice plates, plastic sides, plastic door

base.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships 13902-701, both doors fitted.

datasheet.title: Velocity Cable Management product data sheet (Rev.23 06/22)

description: Velocity single-sided vertical cable manager, Chatsworth Products 13902-701: a black plastic and steel manager 70 in (1778 mm) tall and 6 in (152 mm) wide, for 6'H (1.8 m), 38U racks, that bolts to the side of the rack and stands beside it. A back plate carries a wall of T-shaped fingers down each edge, one rack unit apart, and a plastic door in two halves snaps onto their ends over a channel 119 mm wide and 191 mm deep. It takes no rack unit.

gaps.note: the data sheet says openings in the back allow front-to-rear cabling; no held page gives their size or position, so the rear is drawn as a plain back plate with no pass-through.
no held page dimensions a finger: the arm and the head are read by eye from the page 2 drawing, and the count (38 a side) is the rack's units.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side view of one section

gaps.note: the guide says the manager is two sections, equal for 6 ft and 8 ft and a short upper over a long lower for 7 ft; no held page gives the lengths, so the seam is drawn at the middle.
the doors swing open to the right or left and lift off; the format has no hinge, so each is drawn as one fitted plate and the swing is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover

gaps.note: the table's depth includes the bevel of the door, which varies slightly with width; the door is drawn as a flat plate to 249, 8 mm past the 241 the guides reach.
the manager bolts to the rack's upright with M8 bolts; how far it stands from the upright and whether it overlaps the rail is never dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to a rack

gaps.note: the table's notes give the usable width (33 mm less than overall) and the usable depth (191 mm); they do not say that the two finger walls are equal and are all of the 33, or that the 191 runs from the floor to the ends of the guides, so the 16.5 mm wall and the 50 mm behind the floor are derived with those assumptions.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned section of the manager

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.

body.description: the back plate and the two finger walls, left first

door.description: the two half-height doors, the upper first

fingers.description: the T-shaped fingers, the left wall top to bottom and then the right, 38 a side

attrs.note: datasheet - material, finish, colour and the indoor-only statement are the specifications table (page 2) and the table's note 'Color is Black'.

bottom.note: estimated - the bottom end is the top end again.

chassis.note: datasheet - 70 in (1778 mm) high, 6 in (152 mm) wide and 9.8 in (249 mm) deep for 13902-701 in the ordering table. THE DEPTH IS THE TABLE'S, WITH THE BEVEL OF THE DOOR: the table's note says the manager is 9.5 in (241 mm) deep without doors, that the overall depth varies a little with width because of the bevel of the door, and that the usable depth is 7.5 in (191 mm). So the guides end at 241 and the door stands at 249.

color.note: estimated - 'Color is Black' (ordering table); the shade is the near-black of the maker's photographs of the fitted part, which are renders.

door.note: datasheet - two half-height covers that snap onto the T-shaped cable guides, plastic on the 6 in manager. They are drawn as one plate each, the seam at the middle of the height; for the 7 ft manager the installation instructions say the upper section is short and the lower long, and no page gives the lengths, so the seam is estimated there.

fingers.note: estimated - A FINGER TO EACH RACK UNIT, 38 A SIDE. The data sheet says the T-shaped guides are 'spaced 1U apart' and the installation instructions show a column down each edge; no page counts them. 38 is the rack's units (6'H (1.8 m), 38U), a column centred on the height with 44.45 left at each end. A finger is an arm 14 high with a head 32 high, read by eye from the page 2 drawing.

floor.note: estimated - the floor of the well is 50 from the rear face: 241 (9.5 in without doors) less the 191 usable depth (7.5 in). This takes the usable depth to run from the floor to the ends of the guides, which the table's note does not say.

front.note: estimated - the doors, fitted. With them off the front is the channel between the two finger walls, the ends of the fingers along each edge and the back plate at the bottom of it. The channel is 119 wide, the 152 overall less the 33 (1.3 in) the table's note takes off for the usable width, so each wall is 16.5 if the two walls are equal and are all of the 33, which no held page says.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on the front view is the channel between the two finger walls, 119 wide, run down the height (`run: y`). Its finger pitch is the rack unit, 44.45; the gap between arms is the pitch less the arm's estimated 14.

left.note: estimated - the side, rear at x=0: the back plate, the wall root, 38 arms and heads at one rack unit and the door, with the seam between the two halves.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET TABLE; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM THE INSTALLATION DRAWINGS. The Velocity Cable Management product data sheet (Rev.23 06/22) (page 3) prints the part as 70 x 6 x 9.8 in (1778 x 152 x 249 mm), shipping weight 19 lb (8.2 kg) as printed, for 6'H (1.8 m), 38U racks, with notes on depth and usable size. The Velocity Vertical Cable Manager installation instructions (IIS-713902, Rev. 2) draw how it is assembled, mounted and fitted with its doors. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: a finger, the root of a wall, the door section and the position of the rear openings are estimated, each in its own entry below. Nothing was copied from a picture; the figures are transcribed.

mount.note: drawing - rack-side. The installation instructions (pages 1 and 4) have the manager positioned next to the rack and bolted to the rack's upright with M8 bolts through the manager's holes and the rack's front holes ('the top front rack hole'), eight M8 x 25 mm bolts in the kit, so it stands beside the rack, outside the rails, its fingers facing forward. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 38` is the rack it is sold for ('For 6'H (1.8 m), 38U Racks').

rear.note: estimated - the data sheet says 'openings in the back of the manager allow easy front-to-rear cabling' and the photographs show them, but no held page dimensions or positions any. The rear is drawn as the plain back plate with its seam; the openings are a gap.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides.

shell.note: drawing - a hollow manager, as every manager in the library is. The body is a sheet body and its views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: the back plate as a well 199 deep, the two finger walls and 76 fingers standing in it, and the two halves of the door, which pull off and open the channel.

thickness.note: estimated - no held page states a wall gauge. 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in the library; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: estimated - the end of the manager seen from above, rear at y=0: the back plate to 50, the wall roots to 60, the arms to 232, the heads to 241 and the door to 249. The depths are the table's; the split is the estimate of the finger and wall.

weight.note: datasheet - 19 lb (8.2 kg) in the ordering table, whose column is SHIPPING weight: the carton is in it, so the manager itself weighs less. It is stated as the weight so the part has one, and is an upper bound. The row's own two figures disagree: 19 lb is 8.6 kg and the table prints 8.2 kg; the kilogram figure is stated as printed.

references.title: Velocity Vertical Cable Manager installation instructions (IIS-713902, Rev. 2)

guides.source: Velocity data sheet page 3 note (usable width) and page 1 (fingers spaced 1U apart); the gap is the pitch less an estimated arm
